_comment: Everything this fork adds UNDER src/, and the qmake project that compiles it.
The build that produces the shipped binaries is qmake (build.sh -> tools/klayout/Dockerfile).
The fork's largest patch by far -- the native SVRF DRC engine, 6,673 lines over 23 commits --
is compiled only because src/buddies/src/bd/bd.pro names its two .cc files by relative path:
src/plugins/tools/svrf_drc/svrf_drc.pro is a deliberately EMPTY subdirs project that exists
only so the src/plugins/tools/tools.pro $$files() auto-glob accepts the folder. That is a
single, easily-broken line of registration in a file upstream also edits, and if it is lost
the tree still configures, still builds, and still ships -- with the engine gone.
check_build_registration.py asserts every `path` below exists AND is named by its `built_by`
project, and -- when the upstream ref is resolvable -- that this manifest still covers every
source the fork adds under src/. `cpp_tests` is the list run_cpp_unit_tests.sh feeds to
ut_runner, checked the same way against the TEST()s the fork adds.

sources.why: the SVRF/Calibre-syntax DRC engine itself; compiled into klayout_bd for the svrfdrc buddy
the `svrfdrc` buddy entry point -- the only shipped artefact that reaches the engine
carries the fork's only C++ guard (see cpp_tests); upstream owns the rest of the file
carries the fork's fill_margin guards (see cpp_tests); upstream owns the rest of the file

cpp_tests.guards: a5a7a2d6b -- DeepShapeStore split lines reported as real polygon edges by two-layer checks
cpp_tests.also_probed_by: vibeic-tests/deep_split_line_probe.py, which needs no build and so reaches the shipped image

cpp_tests.guards: fill_margin was not applied BETWEEN the locally-anchored fill arrays of neighbouring polygons of one fill region -- fill_region_impl fills each merged polygon independently and nothing separated the resulting different-origin arrays
the same defect through fill_region_repeat, i.e. Cell#fill_region_multi -- the method whose documentation carries the 'safety distance between pitch-incompatible arrays' promise
